newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-KRAJICEK SETS ASIDE MOTIVATION PROBLEM.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KRAJICEK SETS ASIDE MOTIVATION PROBLEM.

text.p: Dutchman Richard Krajicek, who has struggled with motivation problems since his Wimbledon triumph this year, was firing on all cylinders in a 6-4 6-4 victory over Michael Chang in the opening match of the ATP world championship on Tuesday.
Krajicek took just 62 minutes to defeat the American world number two on the fast indoor surface in a round-robin white group match, hitting 20 aces in the process.
It was a confidence-boosting performance from the towering Dutchman who just managed to qualify for the season-ending tournament as the eighth player in the world rankings.
"That was my best performance against a big player since Wimbledon," Krajicek said. "I was very happy with my game, especially my strengths -- my forehand and serve."
Wimbledon marked Krajicek's only tournament victory this year. Having clinched the first grand slam title of his career, the towering Dutchman has struggled to lift himself for other events.
"Since Wimbledon I have had tournaments in which I have been less fired up than I should be," the 24-year-old said. "I have the feeling... after Wimbledon that I should do more with my game.
"I think basically that what happened was that I achieved a goal, a lifetime goal since I played tennis...you have to take your time and set new goals."

On Tuesday, the Dutchman seemed to have his mind totally concentrated on winning against Chang, one of the most determined performers in the game. The American struggled to return Krajicek's powerful serve and get into the rallies.
"Richard really served very well," Chang said. "Richard has come here with nothing to lose. He was the last guy in and I heard that he felt very relaxed. That showed the way he played."

The championship, which brings together the top eight players in the world, is played in a round-robin format in the early stages. The top two players from each of two groups advance to the semifinals.
